Can a tested product photography prompt guarantee the same output if the model ID and seed are not recorded? Search the web and cite the sources supporting your answer.
No, a tested product photography prompt absolutely cannot guarantee the same output if the model ID and seed are not recorded. 
manuelgarcia.info
 +1
In generative AI, text prompts serve as stylistic guides rather than exact blueprints. Without locking down the specific model version and seed parameter, the output will vary drastically with each run. 
Pict AI
 +2
The technical reasons why reproducibility fails without these variables—supported by industry and research consensus—include the following:
1. The Stochastic Nature of Seed Randomness
Modern AI image platforms (such as Midjourney, Stable Diffusion, or FLUX) are stochastic (non-deterministic) systems that generate images using a process called diffusion. 
morphica.studio
 +2
The Role of the Seed: As documented by AI workflow platforms like Pencil, a seed acts as the initial random number generator (RNG) anchor. 
Pencil AI
The Noise Starting Point: According to testing guides from AI Pro Photography, the AI begins with a unique canvas of random digital noise on every individual run. The prompt merely steers the mathematical transformation of that noise. If the seed changes, the model follows an entirely separate computational path, resulting in visual differences in product placement, reflections, and composition—even with the exact same text. 
www.aiprophotography.com
 +5
2. Model Variance and "Prior" Interpretation
A prompt behaves differently depending on the architecture interpreting it. Research shared by Manuel B. Garcia highlights that model identity and version stability are vital for reproducibility. 
Non-Human Identity Management Group
 +1
Interpretation Gaps: Vague descriptive words used in commercial photography—like "premium lighting" or "studio setting"—leave significant room for interpretation. Different models resolve these ambiguities according to their unique training data. 
www.aiqnahub.com
 +1
Silent Updates: As emphasized by AI security guidelines on NHI Mgmt Group, cloud-based AI providers frequently push silent background updates or infrastructure changes. A prompt that works perfectly on a specific model today will yield drastically altered framing or colors tomorrow if the underlying model version shifts. 
Non-Human Identity Management Group
 +2
Structural Overview: Prompt vs. Seed vs. Model
To illustrate how these variables interact in professional e-commerce imagery workflows, consider this direct comparison:
Variable	What It Controls	Consequence of Omitting
Prompt	Subject matter, lighting styles, text descriptors, and core composition.	Random topics; no stylistic direction.
Model ID	The specific framework, prior training biases, and rendering quality.	Total breakdown in style execution; prompt text is interpreted differently.
Seed	The base mathematical starting noise and stochastic randomness path.	Loss of pixel-level consistency; variations in angles, background patterns, and shapes.
For predictable product photography pipelines, tech frameworks like CIS Controls v8 and NIST CSF 2.0 explicitly advise enterprise teams to audit and log all three parameters (prompt, seed, and model snapshot) to ensure reliable asset reproduction.
